title: Why Asia Is More Enthusiastic About AI Than the West
gist: A short teaser (202 words) presenting Ipsos 2025 survey data showing a roughly two-to-one gap in AI enthusiasm between Asian and Western publics: 84 percent of Chinese and over 80 percent of Southeast Asian respondents are excited or expect profound change, versus 31-40 percent across the U.S., Canada, U.K., and France. The body cuts off before the author's explanation of the gap.

insights.claim: Ipsos 2025 survey data show 84 percent of Chinese respondents said AI-based products and services excited them, versus 38 percent of Americans, 31 percent of Canadians, 37 percent of the British, and 40 percent of the French.
insights.speaker: Akhilesh Pillalamarri
insights.so_what: Consumer AI adoption curves and monetization should run materially faster in Asia than in Western markets; Western AI products face a sentiment headwind that Asian ones do not.
insights.quote: Eighty-four percent of Chinese respondents said that products and services using AI excited them.
insights.locator: According to a survey conducted by Ipsos in 2025

insights.claim: Over 80 percent of respondents in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Singapore said AI will profoundly change their lives within the next few years.
insights.speaker: Akhilesh Pillalamarri
insights.so_what: Southeast Asia is a receptive market for AI-enabled services and a lower-friction environment for AI deployment in consumer finance, health, and government services.
insights.locator: over 80 percent of respondents from the Southeast Asian countries

insights.claim: Enthusiasm for AI tracks a non-Western versus Western split rather than a purely income or development split, with 65 percent of Indians, 67 percent of Turks, and 69 percent of South Koreans expressing excitement despite South Korea being a high-income economy.
insights.speaker: Akhilesh Pillalamarri
insights.so_what: Wealth does not predict AI receptivity — segment AI go-to-market by cultural attitude, not GDP per capita.
insights.quote: surveys consistently show that Asians — and in fact, most non-Western populations — are much more enthusiastic and excited about AI than people from the West

insights.claim: AI is increasingly seen as vital to national economic growth and national security, with LLMs such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude now ubiquitous in daily life while spreading trepidation about relationships and employment.
insights.speaker: Akhilesh Pillalamarri
insights.so_what: The framing of AI as a national-security asset supports continued state-backed AI capex across Asia regardless of near-term commercial returns.
insights.locator: We are living in the age of artificial intelligence
